theorem.setup: Let F be an explicit complete finite requirement universe and let S be any hidden load-bearing subset of F. Assume the evaluator only penalizes misses or violations on S with nonnegative penalties.
theorem.statement: If the Brain proves zero misses and zero violations on every element of F, then it attains the evaluator ceiling for every admissible hidden subset S and every nonnegative weighting over S.
theorem.consequence: The hidden relevance or materiality classifier is unnecessary once a stronger complete-superset ceiling is proved.

requirements: F is independently proved complete for the claimed task instance or scope.
All hidden load-bearing requirements are subsets of F.
The evaluator is monotone nonincreasing in misses or violations and has no reward for omitting elements of F.
Brain actually proves zero misses or violations over F under the same hard constraints.
falsifiers: A load-bearing evaluator dimension is not represented in F.
The evaluator rewards selective omission or penalizes preserving a nonrelevant element.
F completeness is only sampled or heuristic.
Brain coverage of F is incomplete.
hard_nonclaims: No current terminal predicate is closed.
No claim a complete F has yet been proved for finance.
No terminal acceptance family capability or ownership credit.
